analysis.summary: Ivory Coast and Norway meet in the World Cup Round of 32 for the first time ever in competitive football. Norway arrive as clear favourites, powered by Erling Haaland's four-goal group-stage haul, while Ivory Coast are making their maiden knockout appearance in World Cup history. Norway's manager strategically rested Haaland and key players against France (a 4-1 defeat) to ensure full freshness for this tie, making their real form from the first two group games — a 4-1 win over Iraq and 3-2 win over Senegal — the true benchmark. Ivory Coast were solid and organised under Emerse Fae, going 6 points from 3 games with a +1 goal difference, but their attacking output was modest: three goals across the group, largely built on defensive structure rather than firepower.
analysis.home_form: Ivory Coast finished second in Group E with 6 points: beat Ecuador 1-0 (Amad Diallo, late), lost 2-1 to Germany (Kessie scored, conceded in stoppage time), beat Curacao 2-0 (Pepe brace). Total: 3 goals scored, 2 conceded. Defensively disciplined in a 4-3-3 under Fae. Key attackers: Nicolas Pepe (2 goals), Amad Diallo (1 goal), Yan Diomande. Midfield anchor: Franck Kessie and Ibrahim Sangare. Making their first-ever World Cup knockout appearance.
analysis.away_form: Norway finished second in Group I with 6 points: beat Iraq 4-1 (Haaland brace), beat Senegal 3-2 (Haaland brace, Pedersen goal), lost to France 4-1 (fully rotated squad, Haaland unused substitute — result irrelevant to form assessment). Real form in competitive play: 7 goals scored, 3 conceded in two meaningful matches. Haaland has 4 World Cup goals in just 2 games (59 international goals overall in 52 caps). Odegaard provides creativity. Norway operating in a 4-3-3. Returned to knockout stages for first time since 1998.
analysis.h2h: No previous competitive head-to-head meetings on record between Ivory Coast and Norway. This is their first competitive encounter at a World Cup.
injuries_news: Ivory Coast: Wilfried Singo (centre-back, Galatasaray) is a doubt with a hamstring injury suffered before the Curacao game; expected to miss or be a late fitness test. Odilon Kossounou and Ousmane Diomande likely to partner in central defence.

Norway: Julian Ryerson (right-back, Borussia Dortmund) is a doubt after missing training with a thigh injury; if unavailable Fredrik Aursnes may shift to right-back with Patrick Berg entering midfield.
Erling Haaland: fit and fully rested — did not feature against France (rested by Solbakken deliberately for the knockouts).
key_factors: Haaland fully rested with 4 goals in 2 games — the most dangerous individual player in the tournament.
AT&T Stadium is a climate-controlled indoor dome — negates the Texas heat that caused Norwegian cramping in group stage and removes a potential Ivory Coast advantage.
Norway's defensive record was 7 goals conceded in Group I, but 4 came in the heavily rotated France game; their first-choice backline conceded 3 in two wins.
Ivory Coast's attacking output was modest (3 goals, 2 coming against weakest group opponent Curacao); their style is transition-based and they may cede possession.
No competitive head-to-head history creates genuine uncertainty around match dynamics.
Ivory Coast are historically in a first knockout match (historic milestone) while Norway have only ever lost their two previous World Cup knockout games.
Market and Opta simulation both strongly favour Norway (Opta: 56.1% Norway win in 90 minutes vs 21.6% Ivory Coast win).
Norway haven't kept a clean sheet in 10 international matches — Ivory Coast's pacey wingers Amad Diallo and Yan Diomande could exploit that.

value_notes: Market-implied probabilities (after removing overround of 5.6%): Ivory Coast 0.271, Draw 0.279, Norway 0.451. My model probabilities: Ivory Coast 0.24, Draw 0.27, Norway 0.49. My Norway probability (0.49) exceeds the market-implied (0.451) by 0.039 — below the 0.05 edge threshold, no qualifying edge on Norway. My Ivory Coast probability (0.24) is below market (0.271), so no edge there either. On totals: market implies over 2.5 at 50.8% (1/1.97); my estimate is 50% — no meaningful edge. On btts: market implies btts_yes at 59.9% (1/1.67); my estimate is 50% — model is 9.9 percentage points BELOW the market, suggesting btts_no (odds 2.25, implied 44.4%) may carry value if my assessment of Ivory Coast's modest attack is correct (edge vs market: ~0.50 vs 0.444 = 0.056, marginally above 0.05 threshold on the NO side). No single market clears a clean 0.05 edge on the favoured side with high confidence; the clearest divergence is btts_no where I estimate Norway may be more likely to keep a clean sheet than the market prices suggest given Ivory Coast's limited attacking output.
